units: <cite ref="Targum of I Chronicles 12:38">Targ. I Chr. XII, 38</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 55a:4">Ab. Zar. 55ᵃ</cite> <he>לִבִּי ולִבָּךְ ידע</he> myself and thyself are convinced &c.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 7:8">Midr. Till. to Ps. VII</cite> (ref. to <he>תשמרם</he>, <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 12:8">ib. XII, 8</cite>) <he>נטר אורייתא בלִבְּהוֹן וכ׳</he> guard the Law in their hearts.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 28:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. XXVIII</cite>, end (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 37:4">Gen. XXXVII, 4</cite>) <he>מה דבל׳ הוי בפומא</he> as they thought so did they speak, but there (<cite ref="II Samuel 13:22">II Sam. XIII, 22</cite>) <he>מה דבל׳ לא בפומא</he> he did not speak out what was in his heart; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 84:19">Gen. R. s. 84</cite> <he>די בלִיבְּהוֹן בפומהון</he>; <he>די בלִיבֵּיה בליביה</he> what was in his heart remained there.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 35a:11">Snh. 35ᵃ</cite> [read:] <he>נהי דפומא כתבין ל׳ דאינשי אינשי</he> although they (the secretaries) record the word of mouth (the vote of each judge), the heart (the impressiveness of the argument), once forgotten, remains forgotten (cannot be recalled several days after; v. Rashi in Rabb. D. S. a. l. note).

<cite ref="Chullin 59a:4">Ḥull. 59ᵃ</cite>, a. fr.—<he>אַלִּ׳ ריקנא</he> on an empty stomach; a. v. fr.—<he>אַלִיבָּא ד־</he> (<he>אַלִּיבֵּיה</he>), v. <cite ref="A01838"><he>אַלִּיבָּא</he></cite>.—Pl. <he>לִבַּיָּא</he>, <cite ref="L00405"><he>לִיבַּ׳</he></cite>, <he>לְבָבַיָּא</he>, <he>לִבְבַיָּא</he>, <cite ref="L00110"><he>לִבְבִין</he></cite>, <he>לִבְבֵי</he>, <cite ref="L00031"><he>לִי׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 27:19">Targ. Prov. XXVII, 19</cite> <he>לִבַּיָּא</he> (ed. Lag. <he>לִבֵּיהוֹן</he>).
